title: Transmission-acceleration dengue outbreak-detection pipeline: a step-by-step computational protocol
author: Keanu John Pelitro

steps.title: Prepare Quezon City Data and STA/LTA Series
steps.instruction: Load the 'QC Data' sheet from the workbook and build the STA/LTA ratio series.

substeps.instruction: Index each row to the Monday of its ISO week using columns YR, WN, and DC_QC.
Build a right-aligned four-week short-term average (STA).
Build a twenty-six-week long-term average (LTA) separated by a two-week guard band.
Calculate the ratio of the STA to the LTA.
Use reported cases as supplied without back-calculation to symptom-onset date.

steps.title: Define Evaluable Years
steps.instruction: Filter the dataset to retain only evaluable years for Quezon City.

substeps.instruction: Drop COVID-19 surveillance-disruption years (2020 and 2021).
Drop the truncated 2025 year.
Retain the 10 evaluable seasons from 2013 to 2019 and 2022 to 2024.

steps.title: Screen Regional Panel Data
steps.instruction: Load and filter the regional dataset for evaluability.

substeps.instruction: Read the 'Regional Data' sheet.
Fold Region IV-B into MIMAROPA.
Apply the same year exclusions used for the city data.
Retain a region for a given year only if its annual peak reaches at least 12 cases.

steps.title: Compute Rolling Week-Specific Outbreak Threshold
steps.instruction: Calculate the outbreak threshold for each calendar week using the 'QC Data' sheet.

substeps.instruction: For each calendar week, calculate the threshold as the mean plus two standard deviations of cases in the same ISO week across the rolling baseline.

steps.title: Define Vaezi-style Detector
steps.instruction: Implement the Constant Transmission Acceleration detector via the run_vaezi() function.

substeps.instruction: Set the detector to activate when the STA/LTA ratio reaches eta_ON.
Freeze the long-term mean at its activation-time value while the detector is on.
Set the detector to deactivate when the ratio falls below eta_OFF.
Release the frozen baseline only after MIN_OFF_RESET (8) consecutive off weeks.

steps.title: Derive Activation Thresholds
steps.instruction: Run six derivation methods (M1-M6) to determine the adopted eta_ON and eta_OFF values.

substeps.instruction: Identify baseline weeks as those with DC_QC below 30% of the annual peak.
Execute M1: baseline-ratio asymmetric quantiles (90th and 50th percentiles).
Execute M2: high-sensitivity ROC operating points (95% and 99% sensitivity via pROC).
Execute M3: ARL calibration to a false alarm average run length of 12 weeks (secondary targets 6 and 26).
Execute M4: leave-one-year-out cross-validation with asymmetric utility favoring early triggering.
Execute M5: negative-binomial theoretical bounds at ±1 standard deviation.
Execute M6: parametric bootstrap of the null STA/LTA ratio (90th and 25th percentiles, 2,000 replicates).
Calculate the raw median across methods to adopt eta_ON = 1.33 and eta_OFF = 0.73.
Write these values to a sourceable file.

steps.title: Verify Effective-Reproduction-Number Mapping
steps.instruction: Confirm the activation threshold corresponds to an effective reproduction number (Rt) just above the epidemic threshold.

substeps.instruction: Approximate the weekly growth rate r as ln(1.33)/13 ≈ 0.022.
Calculate Rt ≈ exp(0.044) ≈ 1.05, assuming a dengue serial interval of approximately two weeks.

steps.title: Build Anticipatory Metrics Framework
steps.instruction: Establish anchors for evaluating trigger accuracy and timeliness.

substeps.instruction: Define Anchor A1 (Pre-peak Actionable Window): weeks from peak minus 8 to peak minus 4.
Define Anchor A2 (Epidemic Burden block): the smallest contiguous block containing the peak with cumulative cases ≥ 70% of the annual total.
Classify a trigger at week t as a 'true alarm' if t is in A1 or A2; otherwise, if lead is ≥ 9 weeks, it is a 'false alarm'.
Use the global annual maximum as the single peak for aggregate tables (exception: 2024 bimodal year uses two peaks at week 34 and 47 for Figure 3).

steps.title: Run Eleven-Detector Bank
steps.instruction: Execute the full suite of detectors using prospective walk-forward construction for percentile and SD-based metrics.

substeps.instruction: Transmission-acceleration paradigm: Constant TA (run_vaezi), Continuous TA, Composite Outbreak Signal, Critical Transition Indicator, Incidence Gradient, and Hydrological Inflection Measure.
Retrospective-threshold paradigm: Outbreak Threshold (mean + 2 SD), Alarm Threshold (mean + 1 SD), and walk-forward CUSUM.
Surveillance-guideline percentile paradigm: WHO 90th Percentile Threshold and WHO 75th Percentile Threshold.

steps.title: Score Metrics
steps.instruction: Evaluate the detectors across three categories using the count of evaluable years as the denominator (substitute 0 for non-firing years).

substeps.instruction: Burden and accuracy: TAM (True-Alarm Magnitude), N_True_Alarms, PPV, and Sensitivity (A1-restricted).
Timeliness: Mean_Lead_Time, WP (Warning Persistence), and ALY (Actionable Lead-Time Yield).
False alarms: N_False_Alarms.

steps.title: Perform Head-to-Head Comparison
steps.instruction: Compare Constant TA, Continuous TA, and Outbreak Threshold detectors.

substeps.instruction: Conduct paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (alpha = 0.05).
Report year-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals (B = 2,000 for headline) and Wilcoxon P values.
Generate sensitivity tables S1, S3, and S5 by varying Actionable Window width, Epidemic Burden cumulative-case fraction, and year-inclusion rules.

steps.title: Compute Regional Bootstrap Dominance
steps.instruction: Calculate the probability of detector dominance per region.

substeps.instruction: Perform year-cluster bootstrap replicates (B = 1,000, seed 20260101).
Rank the three target detectors on the five primary metrics.
Average the ranks to find the composite mean rank and record the leader for each replicate.
Calculate Pr as the proportion of replicates in which a detector leads.

steps.title: Classify Regional Consensus Tiers
steps.instruction: Categorize regions based on head-to-head checks.

substeps.instruction: Classify as strong consensus, partial consensus, lead only, or contested.
Apply strict cross-stratum Bonferroni correction (k = 51).
Use Pr ≥ 0.75 as the decisive zone convention.
Output Figure 4 multipanels, Figure 5, and regional CSVs.

steps.title: Process Country Panel Data
steps.instruction: Repeat the dominance and consensus analysis at the country scale.

substeps.instruction: Read 'Country Data' sheet and apply the same evaluable-year criteria (5 to 7 years per country).
Compute bootstrap dominance probability and consensus tiers (B = 1,000, seed 20260101).
Apply strict cross-stratum Bonferroni correction (k = 24).

steps.title: Inspect Seasonality and Finalize Outputs
steps.instruction: Verify the seasonality precondition and render final results.

substeps.instruction: Confirm seasonality for each country (e.g., Colombia as the aseasonal diagnostic case).
Render Figure 6 multipanels, Figure 7, and country CSVs.
Render Figure 1 panels (a) including pandemic years and (b) excluding 2020-2021.
Export fig1_dengue_thresholds_vertical.pdf/.png (600 dpi) and corresponding .csv files to Stage2_outbreak_threshold_drift_QC/.
